topic: How do GEO vs LEO satellite orbits affect latency and coverage in hybrid networks for rural substation monitoring?
response: GEO satellites exhibit significantly higher latency (round trip delay) due to their geostationary orbit, exceeding the latency of terrestrial networks. LEO satellites, with lower orbital altitudes, offer drastically reduced latency, comparable to terrestrial networks. This reduction in latency directly translates to improved performance in rural substation monitoring with faster data transmission and reduced delays in communication.
reference_context: Satellite communication systems can provide seamless wireless coverage so as to complement and extend terrestrial communication networks and, as in recent standardization endeavors, are expected to be incorporated in future wireless networks, in particular 5g and beyond networks.  LEO satellite communications, with orbits at altitudes of less than 2000 km, have recently gained broad research interests due to the potential in providing global wireless access with enhanced data rates.
